text:
Pavel Zacha has 14 points in 17 games and a four-game point streak, and Daily Faceoff counted him and David Pastrnak among the league's best duos. The Hockey Writers went the other way and argued Boston should sell high. Our numbers lean toward the second view, for one reason.

Boston has scored 10 more goals than its chances deserve with Zacha on the ice, an on-ice luck figure that rarely lasts. His own shooting is fine (5 goals on 4.2 expected), but the team's finishing around him has been extraordinary, and that's what fills an assist column. At five on five the Bruins get 51% of the expected goals with him on and are three points worse with him than without.

That's not a knock on how he plays. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries and leaving his own zone with possession 64% of the time, the habits of a useful two-way center. Watch the assist rate as the Bruins' shooting comes back to earth: that's where the drop will show.
headline: Zacha's points come with a lot of help
